proposal.description: soft_start's ramp target is floored at the 75% default ceiling, from the package rule that the digital mask must stay above the analog clamp and never be the primary limiter, so a host-lowered MAX_ON limit is overridden
proposal.reason: If the host writes MAX_ON (0x53) below 37 counts, the next soft start should end with SS_done at the written ceiling and PWM_out pulses cut there. With this fault the ramp keeps climbing to 37, SS_done asserts later, and PWM_out on-times in S_SS and S_RUN stay wider than the host commanded.

proposal.description: fault_arbiter's soft-start trip threshold is floored at the RUN threshold, enforcing the package note that S_SS is 'more tolerant', so a legal host write of trip_ss below trip_run is overridden
proposal.reason: Suppose the host writes TRIP_SS (0x51) below TRIP_RUN, e.g. 5 against 12. An overcurrent in S_SS with 5 to 11 faulted cycles in the window should raise window_trip_SS and send the FSM to S_HICCUP, dropping En and counting a strike. With this fault the converter keeps soft-starting until 12 faulted cycles.

proposal.description: The supervisor's host enable is ORed with the switch-press pulse at the top level, so a fresh press overrides a host disable on the press clock itself. reg_file already restores spi_enable on the next clock, so the override lands a clock early.
proposal.reason: Take a host that has disabled the converter over SPI, and then the switch is pressed. The FSM should leave S_OFF, and En rise, one clock after reg_file registers spi_enable high. With this fault both happen one clock earlier, while CONTROL/STATUS still read spi_enable low.
